newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Kandir confirms CVRD auction on April 29.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Kandir confirms CVRD auction on April 29.

text.p: Brazil's Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said the April 29 privatization auction of state mining concern Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) will not be delayed, a local news agency reported.
Private InvestNews said Kandir, speaking on local TV Globo, also confirmed that Vale's 3.0 billion reais minimum price will not be altered.

Kandir told the television the auction would go ahead despite a high court injunction suspending the transfer of 411,000 hectares of mineral properties in the Carajas mining area in the northern state of Para, the agency said.
He also said the government has already sent to the Supreme Court all information necessary to have the injunction repealed, InvestNews added.
Carajas is CVRD's main asset and the prize investors are seeking in their bid to buy the 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD.
Newspapers today said that sources close to the consortia interested in CVRD said they do not plan to take the risk of bidding at the auction amid a legal dispute.

"We prefer to wait for the Supreme Court's decision. If it is possible to have everything clear before the auction, there is no problem. It is better than buying Vale in the dark. Everything must be clear before the sale," said a source involved in the process.
So far two consortia, one led by Brazilian cement, steel and pulp and paper conglomerate Grupo Votorantim and another led by local private steelmaker CSN, have been formed to bid at the auction.
